raw_final_content:
Three photographs show a small, erect, narrow-leaved herb growing from a disturbed gravel edge. The close views consistently show lanceolate leaves and conspicuous pale hairs on the stem and leaf margins; the lower leaves are broader and partly yellowed or damaged. The wider photograph shows several similar young shoots along the same gravel strip.

The visual pattern is compatible with a fleabane/horseweed in the Erigeron–Conyza group, with E. canadensis, E. sumatrensis and related taxa all plausible. I would stop at Erigeron sp. rather than force a species. The key reason is developmental stage: there are no flower heads, involucres, fruits/pappus or a complete mature branching/leaf series, and those characters are important for separating these very similar ruderal species.

What is strongly grounded in the images is “narrow-leaved, erect, conspicuously hairy juvenile herb.” What is not strongly grounded is a particular species name. The most useful follow-up would be a whole mature plant plus close photographs of flower heads, involucres, upper/lower leaf bases and fruit/pappus.
